questions.0.explain.t: The policy becomes a gate that answers in seconds and is applied equally to everyone.

questions.0.options.0.t: Security rules expressed in an executable language, evaluated automatically on every change

questions.0.options.1.t: A policy manual in a PDF kept under version control

questions.0.options.2.t: A comment in the code explaining the security rules

questions.0.options.3.t: A type of open source license for security tools

questions.1.explain.t: Cases that must pass and cases that must be denied give confidence in the rule.

questions.1.options.0.t: Without tests a rule may stop catching anything, or block legitimate changes

questions.1.options.1.t: Because Rego does not compile unless tests exist

questions.1.options.2.t: To reduce the size of the policy files

questions.1.options.3.t: Because OPA requires tests in order to load the policies

questions.1.q.t: Why test policies written in Rego?

questions.2.explain.t: It is the same ladder as with a WAF: observation, shadow and enforcement.

questions.2.options.0.t: Start in warning mode, measure, fix the legacy and only then block

questions.2.options.1.t: Blocking immediately in production, so nobody breaks the rule

questions.2.options.2.t: Applying only in test environments, forever

questions.2.options.3.t: Creating exceptions with no expiry for every team that complains

questions.2.q.t: What is the healthy way to adopt a new policy without blocking everyone?
